Elise v1.0.9 adds AnyTLS over REALITY. Set the node's security mode to `tls=2` and configure its REALITY settings in the panel; the installer skips certificate setup for these nodes. Certificate TLS (`tls=1`, or an omitted mode) continues to work, and plaintext AnyTLS is rejected.

For AnyTLS + REALITY in V2Board's unified V2Node section, use `--node-type=anytls --panel-type=v2board`. The separate AnyTLS section uses `v2board-uniproxy`; its API currently omits REALITY settings and continues to use certificate TLS. Other panel adapters can use REALITY when their API supplies the security mode and required settings.

The REALITY path uses Elise's shared handshake implementation and retains AnyTLS password authentication, padding, multiplexing, and user limits. Tests cover existing certificate TLS, omitted security modes, invalid settings, fallback probes, and a Go/uTLS client that verifies REALITY certificates and exercises multiple streams, invalid credentials, ALPN, and PROXY protocol v1/v2.

This release also includes the installation and maintenance changes made since v1.0.8:

- Add `elisectl purge --yes` and a standalone online uninstall script for removing all standalone Elise instances and their retained data. Ordinary uninstall remains available for recovery without purging configuration and state.
- Default newly generated self-signed certificates to 3650 days.
- Clarify panel selection, node setup, upgrades, and removal in the README.
- Retire automatic V2bX migration while preserving upgrades for existing standalone Elise installations. Existing instance configurations and custom service units continue to work; create new nodes with `elisectl add`.
- Use the `Elise/1.0` user agent for XBoard and V2Board UniProxy requests, including XBoard installation checks. Update any panel or WAF rule matching the previous user agent before upgrading.

Upgrade with `sudo elisectl update`, then verify that `elise --version` reports `1.0.9`. Updating restarts active instances and briefly interrupts their connections; existing configurations, certificates, and traffic state are preserved. Existing certificate TLS nodes do not need configuration changes.

Linux amd64 and arm64 archives include SHA-256 checksums. See the [installation instructions](https://github.com/phungvanquy/elise/blob/v1.0.9/README.md#install-elise) and [certificate and REALITY configuration](https://github.com/phungvanquy/elise/blob/v1.0.9/README.md).
